state.case_summary:
A 67‐year‐old woman was referred for evaluation of a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region. She first noted the lesion two years earlier, with gradual enlargement over the past four months. She denied pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding. Her medical history was notable for hypertension, managed with valsartan/amlodipine, and a hysterectomy in 2016 for abnormal uterine bleeding. She was post‐menopausal, had no history of hormone therapy, and did not smoke or drink alcohol.

On examination, she was afebrile with normal vital signs. Abdominal exam was unremarkable. Inspection revealed a 12 cm, non‐tender mass of the right labia majora extending to the right groin, without erythema, lymphadenopathy, or signs of inflammation. Pelvic exam was otherwise normal.

Soft‐tissue ultrasound showed a well‐defined, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 90 × 44 × 55 mm in the right labia majora tracking into the inguinal canal, with mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging. Routine laboratory results, including blood counts and metabolic panel, were within normal limits. The leading preoperative impression was a canal of Nuck hernia containing omental tissue.
